reviews.body:
### 🟡 Changes recommended A critical regression allows a pod-policy exception to overwrite the node’s allow entry with deny-all, potentially blocking node-to-pod traffic, including kubelet probes.
1 open issue - [Restore node-host allowance after encoding pod-policy exceptions](https://github.com/aws/aws-network-policy-agent/pull/769#discussion_r4529408888) · New
What changed in this PR Addresses #749 by distinguishing node-host CIDRs from broader networks, so policy rules are not dropped when their network address equals the node IP. **Changes:** - Restricts `IsNodeIP` matches to valid `/32` and `/128` host CIDRs. - Adds helper and rule-filtering tests for host addresses, broader networks, and invalid input. - Adds regression checks that pod and cluster policy maps retain the affected network key. | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | `pkg/​utils/​utils.go` | Requires a valid host-length prefix before matching the node IP. | | `pkg/​utils/​utils_test.go` | Tests IPv4, IPv6, network-range, and invalid-CIDR classification. | | `pkg/​fwruleprocessor/​fw_rule_processor_test.go` | Tests filtering and network-key retention in both policy processors. |
Review effort: Balanced

review_comments.body: For node `10.0.1.0`, retaining a pod-policy rule for `10.0.1.0/24` with `Except: ["10.0.1.0/32"]` now causes `ComputeMapEntriesFromEndpointRules` to overwrite the node's allow entry with a deny-all exception. This can block node-to-pod traffic, including kubelet probes, when no cluster-policy allowance overrides it. Keep the broader rule, but restore the node-host allowance after encoding policy entries in `pkg/fwruleprocessor/fw_rule_processor.go`, and add a regression asserting the node entry's value rather than only its key.
